result.markdown: --- title: "[duration()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Describe a time as the elapsed time between two date or datetime columns. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ingest.py#L152-L208){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python duration( start, end, *, unit="days", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Study exports often record calendar dates (enrollment, last contact, death) rather than durations. `duration()` names the two columns and the time unit, and Greenwood computes the difference when it reads the data. Pass the result as the `time` (or `time2`) argument of an `Outcome` constructor. Inside a formula, write `duration(enroll, exit, unit="years")` instead. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [start]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column holding the origin, such as an enrollment date. [end]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The column holding the exit, such as the date of the event or of last contact. [unit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["days"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The time unit: `"days"` (the default), `"weeks"`, `"months"`, `"years"`, `"hours"`, `"minutes"`, or `"seconds"`. Months and years use average lengths (30.4375 and 365.25 days). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Duration]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A frozen `Duration` spec holding the two column names and the unit. It is computed when the data is read, and it prints as the call that made it, such as `duration(start='enroll', end='exit', unit='days')`. The `Duration` class is exported for type annotations. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Compute follow-up time in years from two date columns: ::: {#b65d8026 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw import polars as pl from datetime import date study = pl.DataFrame({ "enroll": [date(2021, 3, 1), date(2021, 3, 15), date(2021, 4, 1)], "exit": [date(2022, 1, 10), date(2021, 9, 22), date(2023, 1, 1)], "outcome": ["died", "censored", "died"], }) # The time is the gap between the two dates, in years gw.Outcome.surv( time=gw.duration(start="enroll", end="exit", unit="years"), event="outcome == 'died'", ).bind(study) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Surv(type=right, n=3, events=2) ``` ::: ::: The same response written as a formula, fitted with `data=`: ::: {#bfb6c327 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} gw.KaplanMeier().fit( "Surv(duration(enroll, exit, unit='years'), outcome == 'died')", data=study ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` KaplanMeier (Kaplan-Meier survival estimate) n events median 0.95LCL 0.95UCL 3 2 0.8624 0.8624 NA ``` ::: :::
